interest: Shows postwar Japan's economic recovery planning under Tsuru, reliant on US aid and a shift from silk to machinery exports.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.50 Five-Year Plan) covers U.S. diplomatic and occupation reporting between February and October 1948 on Japanese government planning for post-World War II economic recovery and self-sufficiency. The primary document is Despatch No. 106 from William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, which forwards and reviews a confidential summary of the 'Five-Year Plan for Japan's Economic Rehabilitation' prepared by the Economic Stabilization Board under Deputy Secretary-General Shigeto Tsuru. The plan sets economic targets for 1948 through 1952 aimed at restoring pre-war (1930–1934) standards of living, curbing inflation, revitalizing coal and power generation, shifting exports toward heavy machinery and Asian markets, and balancing international payments with substantial American aid and credit. The file concludes with an October 1948 telegram from Shanghai quoting Chinese press reports on Japan's five-year targets for multiplying chemical industry output, highlighting regional attention to Japan's economic revival.

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting and analyzing an advance summary of the Japanese Economic Stabilization Board's Five-Year Plan for Economic Rehabilitation.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: U.S. Political Adviser William J. Sebald transmits to the Secretary of State a confidential summary of the Five-Year Plan for Japanese Economic Rehabilitation prepared by the Economic Stabilization Board of the Prime Minister's Office. Handed over by Deputy Secretary-General Shigeto Tsuru, the plan seeks to achieve pre-war living standards and balance international payments by 1952 despite population growth. Sebald highlights the parallel planning by SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section, the domestic obstacles of inflation and energy shortages, and Japan's estimated foreign assistance requirements of over 1.6 billion dollars.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 106 from Tokyo transmitting Economic Stabilization Board's Five-Year Plan summary

subfiles.about: A Japanese government summary report detailing targets, sectoral projections, and balance-of-payments estimates for economic recovery from 1948 through 1952.
subfiles.from: Economic Stabilization Board, Prime Minister's Office, Japanese Government
subfiles.summary: This confidential summary sets forth the quantitative requirements to achieve a balanced and self-sustaining Japanese economy by 1952. It details projections for population growth, real national income recovery, mining and manufacturing supply (notably coal and electric power), staple food production and rationing, and labor force employment. The document emphasizes that initial efforts in 1948–1949 must curb inflation and restore power and transport before expanding general industrial exports, and it calculates a need for 1,631 million dollars in foreign long-term aid plus 300 million dollars in revolving credit.
subfiles.title: The Five Year Plan for Japan's Economic Rehabilitation (Summary)
subfiles.to: Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ, SCAP / Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.about: An incoming telegram conveying a Chinese press report on Japanese production targets for chemical and heavy industrial commodities through 1953.
subfiles.summary: Shanghai relays a 1948 report on Japan's five-year plan to quadruple chemical production, including soda, cement, and glass.
